round: architect-scoped round: does the kept-decision property model cover every real transition, and does every person's decision reach the controller once and the current architect once, none lost; plus the release rule, the tester's red test, and review 5705826477's findings
accepted: Review 5705826477's five findings are fixed: keepStaleApproval keeps the pair on a nil gate under an armed gate (admit.go:965-980); claimed_by stops a catch-up naming what a queued start names; DeliveredRows stops a retried start re-sending after its delivery retired; parkDecision logs one line per outcome and the verdict jq matches; TestOnlyADeliveredStartForgetsTheDecisionsItNamed fails without the start's forget.
The release rule (HandOverKept) and the tester's red test hold: a stale start's release reaches the running architect once.
RootHears leaves main's resume paths unchanged: ResumeAwaitedRoot's two paths, fresh admission and re-admission all hold a slot when their task is sent (root_hears_main_paths_test.go:474).
The model's declared exclusions hold: a retired claim keeps its pending task (retire writes the claim only); a death mid-turn re-sends the same delivery; nothing is kept for an awaiting_person root.

keyFindings.description: A catch-up dropped while it is publishing tells its decisions twice. DropCatchUps deletes a leased catch-up that has no kept-told mark yet; the FK frees its claims and the same transaction's new catch-up claims them; the first publish then succeeds and forgets only rows it still claims, and the second catch-up tells them again. The model runs rows one at a time, so it never interleaves a publish with a ready or a settlement.

After a restart, a held start task (RootHears false, never sent) on a Ready/Idle claim is confirmed by askFirst when the agent is streaming, or by turnStarted's inFlight on a foreign turn, then retired at the turn's end. Its decisions were forgotten when the claim queued it, so they are lost. The model's fake conn never streams and its turn step fires only for an acknowledged task.

Decisions kept on a child are stored under the child's root (record/parked_decision.go:96). The orphan hand-over carries the child's gate and pull request but not those rows, so the child's new tree's architect never hears them. The model has no hand-over transition.

A catch-up whose receipt timed out and that a newer catch-up has superseded is not re-held, and its row finishes, so the deletion releases its claims. Nothing hands them over, though the architect hears and no ready is coming, so the decisions wait for an unrelated relaunch. deliverNotice's superseded branch hands over (outbox.go:705-716); this one should too.

KeptToldSource's comment says the mark goes under the catch-up's own row key. toldKept marks under the Published key, which a re-held copy shares with its original, and DropCatchUps' SQL computes that key. Fix the comment.

notFindings: Code-quality's point that the model's decide() keeps on the claim-level rule (nobodyHears=true) while the ask path uses root.Lingers() is not a fault. The model's states are a superset: they are the outbox path's keep. The ask path's keep rule is pinned by the admit tests.

Three readings of 'who hears' (outbox claim-level, ask path linger-only, ArchitectHears for the hold and hand-over) differ only for a running tree whose architect claim ended. That tree is not parked, which is outside this issue's scope. The ArchitectHears comment overstates it as the only reading.

A held g1 task sent in g2 names the stale approval pair kept at g1. The architect requests approval of what Dispatch shows, and register_gate takes the newer of the caller's and Dispatch's version, so nothing is lost or told twice.
kept_decision_property_test.go is a new 1,236-line test file, and settleKept's gave flag is redundant with DeliveredRows. These are maintainability items, not faults.
